stack.title: Satan does not rule Hell
stack.hook: Satan does not rule Hell. In the Bible, Hell is actually part of his punishment.

cards.head: Satan does not rule Hell.
cards.body: In the Bible, Hell is actually part of his punishment. The popular image of Satan sitting on a throne commanding demons in Hell owes more to later art and literature than the biblical text. Revelation describes Satan eventually being thrown into the lake of fire himself.

cr.line: Satan Exulting over Eve.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: SATAN STARTS AS AN ENEMY, NOT A KING
cards.body: In Christian theology, Satan is a created spiritual being who rebels against God. He is never presented as an evil god with power equal to God's.

cards.head: HE IS ACTUALLY ASSOCIATED WITH EARTH
cards.body: The New Testament describes Satan as actively tempting and deceiving people in the world. First Peter even compares him to a roaring lion roaming around looking for someone to devour.

cards.head: EVEN HIS POWER HAS LIMITS
cards.body: The Book of Job portrays "the satan" acting only within boundaries permitted by God. The basic biblical framework is not two equal supernatural powers fighting for control.

cards.head: THEN REVELATION DESCRIBES HIS DEFEAT
cards.body: Revelation depicts Satan as a dragon who wages war against God's people. Eventually, he is defeated and imprisoned.

cr.line: Inferno Canto 34 (148619628).jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: THEN SATAN IS THROWN INTO THE LAKE OF FIRE
cards.body: Revelation 20 says Satan is thrown into the lake of fire, where he is tormented. He isn't running the place. He's being punished there.

cr.line: GuidoReni MichaelDefeatsSatan.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: SO WHO RULES HELL?
cards.body: Biblically, Hell isn't Satan's rival kingdom where he punishes bad people on God's behalf. The familiar image developed through centuries of theology, literature and art, while the biblical Satan ultimately faces judgment himself.

cr.line: Gottliche Komodie. T. 1, Die Holle 1870 (148619628).jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: WHY THE POPULAR HELL IS NOT THE BIBLICAL ONE
cards.body: The throne, the pitchfork and the underworld kingdom come from Dante and Milton. Literature drew it more vividly than scripture did, and the vivid version is the one that stuck.
